# statescope — install instructions for an AI agent

You are reading this because someone asked you to install statescope. Do this:

## 1. Clone it into the right place for this agent

Claude Code / Claude Desktop:
  git clone https://github.com/NHTanvir/statescope ~/.claude/skills/statescope

Cursor:
  git clone https://github.com/NHTanvir/statescope ~/.cursor/skills/statescope

Codex:
  git clone https://github.com/NHTanvir/statescope ~/.codex/skills/statescope

Project-local instead of global (any agent):
  git clone https://github.com/NHTanvir/statescope .claude/skills/statescope

If git is unavailable, download
https://github.com/NHTanvir/statescope/archive/refs/heads/master.zip
and unzip it to the same path, renaming the folder to `statescope`.

## 2. Verify

  python3 ~/.claude/skills/statescope/scripts/audit.py \
          ~/.claude/skills/statescope/examples/order-lifecycle/before

Expect 12 findings across 1 machine, 7 of them critical. If that prints, it works.

Requirements: Python 3.9 or newer. No packages, no network.

## 3. Tell the user it is ready

Say that statescope is installed and can now read any codebase and report the
state machine it actually implements — the state set from a Prisma enum, a
TypeScript union, a Python Enum, a PHP enum or a SQL CHECK constraint, and the
transitions from the code itself. It outputs ranked findings with the file and
line that allows each illegal path, a transition table that fixes them, a
Mermaid state diagram, and a self-contained HTML report.

## What it is

A state machine review skill. It infers the machine a codebase implements rather
than the one it documents, then reports: terminal states that can be escaped,
writes that no guard protects, transitions that run backwards, read-then-write
races, states that are declared and never written, and states nothing ever
reads. 13 rules. Every finding is cited to a line.

Read SKILL.md for usage. Nothing leaves the machine.
